subject: Cloud Computing
title: Serverless Cost Benefits
description: A quick, practical guide to Serverless Cost Benefits.

hook.text: A function runs for 200 milliseconds, once per minute. Serverless charges for those 200 milliseconds only.

buildup.text: Serverless computing bills per execution, not per hour. No traffic means zero cost — the ultimate pay-as-you-go.

discovery.text: For sporadic workloads, serverless can cost 10-100x less than a running server doing the same job.

twist.text: At high volume, serverless gets expensive fast. A constantly running Lambda costs more than an EC2 instance.

climax.text: Serverless is cheapest for bursty, unpredictable traffic. For steady loads, traditional compute often wins.

punchline.text: Serverless is cheap when idle. Expensive when busy.

quiz.question: When is serverless most cost-effective?
options: For bursty, unpredictable workloads with lots of idle time
For 24/7 high-volume services with constant traffic
Only when used with reserved instance pricing

details.summary: Serverless computing charges per request and execution duration with no cost when idle. For sporadic workloads, this is dramatically cheaper than running always-on servers. But at high and consistent volume, the per-invocation cost can exceed the price of reserved instances.
details.whyItMatters: Serverless economics are counterintuitive. It is the cheapest option for low and variable traffic but can become the most expensive at high sustained volume. Understanding the crossover point is critical.
takeaways: Zero cost when idle with no minimum charges
Per-invocation pricing is expensive at sustained high volume
Cost crossover with instances depends on traffic patterns

faq.question: At what point is serverless more expensive than instances?
faq.answer: The crossover varies by workload, but a rough guideline is when a function runs consistently at high concurrency. If a Lambda function runs 24/7 at steady load, an equivalent reserved instance can be 5 to 10 times cheaper. The exact breakeven depends on memory and duration.

faq.question: What hidden costs does serverless have?
faq.answer: API Gateway charges, data transfer costs, CloudWatch logging, and the cost of integrating with other services all add up. Cold start latency has an indirect cost in user experience. Monitoring and debugging distributed serverless applications also requires specialized tooling.
